author: GamingBolt
description:
Onimusha: Way of the Sword certainly lives up to its name thanks to how its combat system makes you use your sword to control the direction of the fight. That’s easier said than done against enemies who put up quite a fair fight, and perhaps even overwhelm Musashi’s ironclad defences from time to time. But with the ability to choose what happens with each defensive manoeuvre, and offensive options that make counterattacks all the more devastating, Musashi’s skill set is unique.

But can it carry a title where the story can only do so much to ease the load of expectations that the combat brings? We think that it’s likely, and we’ve got a few reasons why. Join us as we draw blades with Musashi, and show you why his blade is one worth mastering.
title: Is Onimusha: Way of the Sword Building One of the Most Complete Sword-Combat Systems?

author: GamingBolt
description:
With Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 2 drawing ever closer to its August release date, we’ve been itching to give MGS 4 another go, joining Solid Snake on another journey through his later years for the chance to watch him get the ending he deserves yet again. But we think that those among you who aren’t familiar with it are going to find that this one’s not the kind of stealth game you were expecting.

Of course, we’re happy to tell you why we think so. Strap in for a journey through the absolute chaos this game brings to a world built for stealth and action, with the detonator for each gameplay style largely in your hands to mix and match. It’s chaos with a bit of cunning order, and the game encourages the same from you. Here’s why we think so.
title: You Are ABSOLUTELY Not Ready for Metal Gear Solid 4's Return in Master Collection Vol. 2
